title: Human access to production is time-bound and approved
requirement: Standing human access to production namespaces is prohibited. Access is granted just-in-time for a named change or incident, expires within 8 hours, and is approved by someone other than the requester.

title: Workload identity is federated, never a long-lived credential
requirement: Workloads authenticate to cloud services and internal APIs using short-lived federated identity (OIDC / workload identity). Long-lived static credentials issued to a workload are prohibited, including in secret managers.

title: Least privilege on Kubernetes RBAC
requirement: ServiceAccounts are scoped to a single namespace and to the verbs the workload needs. cluster-admin, wildcard verbs and wildcard resources are prohibited outside the platform team's own control-plane tooling.
other_references: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark, RBAC and Service Accounts

title: Break-glass credentials are held offline and alarmed
requirement: Break-glass accounts exist for each production cluster, are stored offline, and every use raises an immediate alert to the on-call security engineer.

title: Mutual TLS on all service-to-service traffic
requirement: Traffic between services inside the platform is mutually authenticated with TLS 1.3. Plaintext internal traffic is prohibited, including within a single cluster or namespace.

title: Customer data is encrypted at rest with bank-managed keys
requirement: Data classified Confidential or above is encrypted at rest using keys held in the bank's own KMS. Provider-managed keys are not acceptable for customer financial data.

title: Certificate lifetimes do not exceed 90 days
requirement: TLS certificates issued by the internal CA expire within 90 days and are renewed automatically. Manual renewal is prohibited for anything in the request path.

title: Secrets are never carried in environment variables or images
requirement: Secrets are mounted from the secret manager at runtime. Secrets in environment variables, container images, Helm values, or git are prohibited regardless of repository visibility.

title: Default-deny network policy in every namespace
requirement: Every namespace carries a default-deny NetworkPolicy for ingress and egress. Permitted flows are declared explicitly and reviewed when they change.
other_references: CIS Kubernetes Benchmark, Network Policies and CNI

title: External exposure goes through the managed edge only
requirement: Services reachable from outside the bank are published through the managed API gateway, which provides authentication, rate limiting, WAF and request logging. Direct LoadBalancer or NodePort exposure of an application is prohibited.

title: Cardholder data environment is network-segregated
requirement: Workloads in PCI scope run in dedicated clusters with no shared network path to non-PCI workloads. Any flow crossing the boundary requires a documented segmentation review.

title: Egress to the internet is allow-listed
requirement: Production workloads reach external destinations through the egress proxy against an allow-list. Unrestricted egress is prohibited.

title: Data classification is declared before a store is provisioned
requirement: Every data store carries a classification (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) and a named data owner before it is created. Undeclared stores are treated as Restricted.

title: Personal and payment data is masked outside production
requirement: Non-production environments never hold real personal or payment data. Data used for testing or analysis is masked, tokenised or synthetic.

title: Personal data does not enter logs, traces or metrics
requirement: Telemetry must not contain personal data, authentication material, primary account numbers or full request or response bodies. Field-level redaction is applied at the emitting service.

title: Customer data stays in the EU
requirement: Customer data is processed and stored within the EU or EEA. Any processing outside requires a transfer assessment approved by the DPO before the change ships.

title: Retention is declared and enforced technically
requirement: Every data store declares a retention period with an enforcing mechanism. Indefinite retention of personal data is prohibited.

title: Security-relevant events are shipped to the central SIEM
requirement: Authentication, authorisation failures, privileged actions and configuration changes are shipped to the central SIEM within 5 minutes and retained 400 days.

title: Audit logs are tamper-evident and separately controlled
requirement: Audit logs are append-only and cannot be modified or deleted by the workloads or operators they describe.

title: New external surfaces have detection before go-live
requirement: A newly exposed external interface has alerting for authentication failure spikes, anomalous volume and error-rate deviation in place before it serves production traffic.

title: Container images are signed and admitted by policy
requirement: Only images signed by the bank's build system are admitted to production clusters, enforced at admission. Images from public registries are mirrored and rescanned first.

title: CI credentials are not shared across teams
requirement: Build credentials are scoped to one team's pipelines. Shared runners must isolate credentials and workspaces per job so one team's build cannot read another's material.

title: Critical and high vulnerabilities are remediated on a clock
requirement: Critical vulnerabilities in production images are remediated within 7 days, high within 30. An unremediated critical past 7 days blocks further deploys of that component.

title: Security-relevant changes carry a recorded risk assessment
requirement: A change that alters an external surface, an authorisation boundary, a data classification, or a cryptographic control carries a documented risk assessment linked to the change record before merge.

title: Production changes are reversible and the rollback is tested
requirement: Every production change has a documented rollback that has been exercised in a pre-production environment.

title: New ICT providers pass third-party risk assessment first
requirement: Any new external ICT service supporting an important business function completes third-party risk assessment and is entered in the register of information before production use.

title: Every provider dependency has a documented exit strategy
requirement: Cloud and SaaS dependencies supporting an important business function carry a tested exit plan, including data extraction format and an estimated migration window.

title: Backups are tested by restore, not by job status
requirement: Backup validity is proven by a restore into an isolated environment at least quarterly. A successful backup job is not evidence of a working backup.

title: Important business functions have stated RTO and RPO
requirement: Services supporting an important business function declare recovery time and recovery point objectives, and the design is demonstrably capable of meeting them.
